A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ActAlign on ActionAtlas, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 ends after its references despite mentioning appendix material; v2 includes Appendices A–E. Newly supplied documentation can be distinguished from retained experiments and relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original ActAlign classification results, component ablations and prompt comparisons on ActionAtlas in Tables 2–4, alongside qualitative alignment analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and additionally reports smoothing-window sensitivity in Appendix A and runtime measurements in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Both versions use LLM-generated sub-action scripts, context augmentation, frozen SigLIP encoders, moving-average smoothing, DTW and path-length-normalized classification scores. V2 explicitly documents the contextualization template and generation prompts; context augmentation was already an evaluated component in v1, so this does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same ActionAtlas coverage: 898 videos, 558 fine-grained actions and 56 sports. V1's SubActionAtlas is described in v2 as an ActionAtlas extension using generated scripts, without changing the videos, labels or classification task. Additional dataset statistics do not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: V1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1 retain the same comparators, including mPLUG-Owl-Video, VideoChat2, VideoLLaMA, LLaVA-Next-Video, Qwen2-VL, X-CLIP and mean-pooled SigLIP, with unchanged baseline scores. Newly discussed methods such as TEAR are not added to the reported evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds a smoothing-window evaluation at w = 10, 20, 30 and 50, with an unsmoothed point also plotted; the default remains 30. V2 removes the explicitly labeled T = 0.2 prompt comparison and leaves the main comparison's generation temperature unspecified. Other retained evaluation settings and Top-1/2/3 metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct smoothing-width sensitivity analysis in Appendix A but removes the explicit T = 1.0 versus T = 0.2 prompt-temperature ablation. Component ablations, context-embedding visualizations, smoothing heatmaps and the skating/skateboarding case studies are retained. Appendix Table 5 supplies scripts for an already illustrated case.

E5.justification: The random baseline still specifies 10 trials, and retained script statistics use the same mean-plus-dispersion reporting. Neither version reports classification confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty for ActAlign. V2's additional descriptive dataset statistics do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The main ActAlign entries change from 30.51/54.34/71.05 in v1 Table 2 to 30.29/53.01/70.27 in v2 Table 1; the DTW-only entries also change. V2's values match v1's T = 1.0 ablation, while the explicit low-temperature rows disappear, so these are not established same-setting performance losses. V2 additionally reports smoothing-sweep outcomes, dataset statistics and a 41.95-second total inference time.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.1 adds an O(NMT) inference-complexity statement in terms of candidate classes, sub-actions and video frames. This is a limited computational-complexity addition; the problem formulation, affinity construction, DTW recurrence and score normalization in Equations 1–14 remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the introduction's empirical contribution from outperforming baselines on fine-grained classification 'benchmarks' to ActionAtlas specifically. The central training-free sequence-alignment contribution, absence of video–text supervision, approximately eightfold parameter comparison and 30.5% abstract headline are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly interprets the smoothing sweep as evidence of low sensitivity to window size and explains the default choice. V2 removes the interpretation that lower generation temperature improves consistency and accuracy. The existing limitations concerning ambiguous scripts and global DTW alignment are retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies exact prompt templates, an explicit context template, checkpoint identification, software versions, RAM, timestamp-based clipping and NumPy processing details, and runtime information, while updating the code address. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Temperature reporting becomes less explicit, and Appendix B's 24GB GPU specification conflicts with the main text's retained 25GB description.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens research positioning through a new action-recognition overview, additional foundational DTW literature and Appendix C's discussion of image–language transfer and methods including TEAR and EZ-CLIP. It also removes the Dynamic Graph Warping discussion. These changes exceed citation metadata corrections or relocation of existing related work.

P1.justification: V2 extensively revises and reorganizes the narrative: related work is recast, SubActionAtlas terminology becomes an ActionAtlas extension, experimental discussion is reordered, and dataset and transfer discussions move into organized appendices. The abstract, method explanations and conclusion are edited, and an author is added.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation. The dataset-generation diagram and script-statistics table move to the appendix, qualitative video examples become filmstrips with rearranged heatmaps, and figures are repositioned within the main text. A smoothing-sensitivity plot, detailed script table and dataset-statistics table are added; retained displays also receive revised labels and captions.

improvement.justification: Appendices B and D materially improve reproducibility by supplying exact prompts and implementation details, while Appendix A adds useful evidence about smoothing sensitivity. These gains are tempered by less clear temperature reporting: the main table now reports 30.29%, while the abstract retains 30.5% and the explicit low-temperature comparison is absent. The net quality improvement is supported but limited by these reporting inconsistencies.
